answer:
1. The animation shows the gap between 15-year and 30-year mortgage rates, using the Freddie Mac weekly survey as its source. Each loan's rate is drawn as a bar. The "stack" shows how far apart the 15-year and 30-year offers sit. A character named Tessa stands by a house with a stack of gold coins or bricks beside it. The frames are labeled "ILLUSTRATIVE", "US only" and "history, not a forecast."

2. The on-screen labels build up one at a time. Frame 1 has no labels. Frame 2 adds "your bar = your loan's own rate." Frame 3 adds "your stack = how far apart the 15-year and 30-year offers sit." A small dashed bar and a document icon also appear next to the dashed figure and tall dashed box. Frame 6 adds "a dollar in the house is hard to get back," and a small lock appears on the house's door. The house, the gold stack and the Tessa figure stay the same throughout.

3. The animation is explaining how to read the graphic: a loan's own rate is a bar, and the gap between the 15-year and 30-year rates is a stack. The final line says money put into a house is hard to get back out, meaning it is illiquid. The lock on the house door reinforces that.

4. The animation gives no explicit instruction. A viewer might take away that extra money paid into a mortgage is locked in the house, so they should weigh that lock-in against the rate gap. That is my reading, and the animation never says it.

5. The only idea the animation put on screen is "a dollar in the house is hard to get back," plus the lock icon. Any advice to pay extra or to invest is my own conclusion, not something the picture or text says. The animation also doesn't say which option is better, and it labels itself as history and not a forecast.
